scope: A bounded raw /dev/nvme0n1 direct-read test bypassing ext4 and the source GGUF, with NVMe/board/battery telemetry captured by the persistent watcher. It reproduces the access failure while approaching the NVMe warning threshold.

test.mode: read-only direct I/O, per-GiB checkpoint and SHA-256

failure.ssh: pre-auth reset/close, same failure signature as prior tests
failure.thermal_signature: temperature climbed from 26.85 C to 85.85 C while chunk time increased from 3 s/GiB to 12 s/GiB

diagnosis.leading: Sustained direct reads cause NVMe thermal runaway and severe throttling; the platform then loses usable access/reset before the device's 87 C warning threshold is durably reported.
support: The raw block-device test bypasses ext4, GGUF parsing, hashing, page cache, and the source file extent map.
The failure reproduced on /dev/nvme0n1 rather than only the model file.
Temperature rose 59 C above baseline and reached 2.15 C below the drive warning threshold.
Throughput fell from about 333 MiB/s to about 83 MiB/s.
Full I/O PSI rose from 0% to 54.35% and one D-state process appeared near failure.
SMART remains clean with zero media errors and zero controller error-log entries, inconsistent with NAND media failure.
likely_contributors: Insufficient SSD heatsink mass, contact pressure, or airflow for a high-power PCIe Gen5 SSD in this laptop
SSD firmware thermal throttling or controller protection
A platform power/EC response to sustained NVMe power draw
A defective thermal interface or marginal SSD controller even though SMART counters are clean
diagnosis.confidence: High for thermal/controller pathway as the immediate trigger; medium for the exact physical root cause.

non_claims: The exact chunk after 60 GiB was not retrievable before SSH failed.
No kernel panic, AER entry, NVMe completion error, or I/O-error line was persisted from the failing instant.
No write test or destructive block operation was run.
The final post-failure SMART snapshot and target progress remain unread until another console recovery.
This does not prove whether insufficient heatsinking, firmware protection, controller malfunction, or platform power response initiates the reset.

checks.name: watcher-telemetry-tests
checks.result: 6 tests passed, including nonblocking hwmon and power-supply parsing.
